overall: The Board violated the Law by approving insufficiently detailed August 24 minutes, already cured by amendment; no violation on the September 14 minutes or September 28 notice; other allegations declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the August 24 meeting minutes were insufficiently detailed because they omitted a member's comments opposing the chair nomination.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board violated the Law by approving insufficiently detailed minutes where the minutes failed to include any mention of the discussion of Mr. Williston’s nomination to the position of chair.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the September 14 minutes were insufficiently detailed because they did not capture a member's changed vote on approving the prior minutes.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the minutes of the September 14 meeting are accurate and sufficiently detailed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board improperly amended the September 28 meeting notice to add a Special Town Meeting article presentation less than 48 hours before the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Absent sufficient evidence that Mr. Williston anticipated discussing the article at the September 28 meeting 48 hours prior to the meeting, we credit the Board’s account of the facts.

allegations.summary: Allegations that the chair deliberated via email and Facebook since July, and the August 24 no-discussion remark, were untimely filed with the Board.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complaint was not filed with the Board until September 29—between 71 and 36 days after the alleged violations were discoverable—we decline to review these allegations.

allegations.summary: Allegations about the chair declining discussion, a member's motion to approve minutes, threatening remarks, and a Facebook page would not violate the Law even if true.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, none of these allegations would constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Additional allegations raised only in the request for further review were not in the original complaint filed with the Board.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review the additional allegations raised in the request for further review because they were not raised in an Open Meeting Law complaint filed with the Board.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
